$comment: FEAT-143 (mkey feat.gameinit): Game Initialization Modes -- Real vs Unlimited Money. The starting treasury balance for `real` mode is data-sourced (never a hardcoded Go literal, per AC-6/GR#15). Spec refs: FEAT-143's own Desc (Real vs Unlimited Money, lock-in on startup, immutable save metadata); docs/METROPOLIS-MASTER-v2.1.md §7 finance/insolvency (line 212); §13 line 12 ('The player starts with money'); §39. The 5,000,000-micropound figure carried in FEAT-143's Desc is a player-felt balance number and is NOT pinned here. BUG-737 (compose wiring) set this figure to £1,500,000 -- matching compose.go's own pre-existing initialTreasury constant (BUG-452's Aaron-ruled dogfood grant) exactly, rather than the earlier 5,000,000 draft placeholder -- so wiring Real mode's opening treasury from this data file reproduces every existing composed-engine test's expectation byte-for-byte (GR#15: never let a data-sourcing refactor silently change player-felt behaviour). Still a disclosed placeholder pending Aaron's row-by-row balance pass; AC-6 checks only that real mode starts with a finite POSITIVE capital and unlimited mode is un-depletable, never this magnitude.

meta.balanceRegime: startingCapitalMicropounds is a disclosed PLACEHOLDER pending Aaron's balance pass -- AC-6 checks direction/shape (finite, positive) only, never this magnitude (GR#15).
